explain.say: At midnight on 6 March 1957, in Accra, Kwame Nkrumah told a huge crowd that Ghana was free for ever. The Gold Coast had become Ghana, the first colony south of the Sahara to win independence. Within about twenty years almost the whole continent followed. Look at the timeline of empire's end.

explain.say: Look at the graph of real counts. In 1950 only four African states were independent. In 1960 alone seventeen new nations were born, so it was called the Year of Africa. By 1980 there were over fifty. Today there are fifty-four, the newest South Sudan in 2011. Can you see the steep jump?

Why then? See the causes. The Second World War weakened Britain and France, and African soldiers came home expecting change. Mass parties, unions and strikes, like Nkrumah's movement in the Gold Coast, pressed hard. The UN and both superpowers opposed old empires, and colonial wars cost lives and money. Which cause came from Africans themselves?

explain.say: Now the map. Some roads were violent. In Algeria, home to about a million European settlers, war from 1954 to 1962 killed hundreds of thousands. In Kenya, Britain crushed the Mau Mau rising with mass detention and torture, for which it paid compensation in 2013. In Congo, the first prime minister, Patrice Lumumba, was murdered in 1961. We remember the victims.

See two paths: negotiation in Ghana, Nigeria and Senegal, armed struggle where many settlers lived, like Algeria, Kenya and Zimbabwe. Frantz Fanon wrote about colonial violence, and Frederick Cooper urged us to see choices, not fate. Excellent work. Challenge: explain why settler colonies fought hardest to keep empire.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Settler colonies saw the longest wars.

faq.q: Why did African countries become independent?
faq.a: African nationalist movements, unions and parties pressed for freedom, while the Second World War had weakened Britain and France, the UN and both superpowers opposed colonial rule, wars in places like Algeria proved costly, and European governments decided colonies were no longer worth holding.
asks: What role did the Second World War play?

faq.q: Why was 1960 called the Year of Africa?
faq.a: Seventeen African countries became independent in 1960, including Nigeria, Senegal, Mali, Congo and Madagascar, most of them former French colonies.

Some transfers, such as Ghana's and Nigeria's, were negotiated after protests and elections. Others involved long wars, especially where many European settlers lived: Algeria, Kenya, Angola, Mozambique and Zimbabwe. The Algerian War killed hundreds of thousands.
asks: What was the Mau Mau uprising?
What happened in the Algerian War?

faq.a: Leader of the Convention People's Party who led the Gold Coast to independence as Ghana on 6 March 1957. A champion of pan-Africanism, he was overthrown in a coup in 1966.

Congo's first elected prime minister was overthrown months after independence in 1960 and killed in January 1961 by Katangan secessionists with Belgian involvement. Belgium admitted moral responsibility in 2002.

facts: Seventeen African countries became independent in 1960.
Algeria became independent in July 1962 after a war that began in 1954.

quiz.say: About 10 African states were independent in 1958 and about 27 by the end of 1960. How many is that in between?
quiz.why: 27 minus 10 equals 17: the seventeen new states of the Year of Africa.

wrong.2: 10 is the starting count, not the change.

quiz.say: Where did decolonisation involve the longest wars?
quiz.why: Settler populations in places like Algeria and Kenya resisted handing over power.

wrong.1: Every colony had some European presence; settler numbers were the key.
